A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniZero and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-F. The expanded scope and reorganized material can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original Atari and VisualMatch experiments, ablations, world-model analyses, and four-game multitask results.

after.justification: v2 reports original Atari, VisualMatch, and DMControl results, including expanded multitask experiments and additional analyses.

M1.justification: v2 adds an implemented continuous-action adaptation: Gaussian policy outputs, sampled MCTS expansion, uniform priors over sampled actions, and visit-weighted policy distillation (Appendix B.3). v1 mentions possible continuous-action embeddings but leaves continuous control to future work. The existing discrete-action architecture and task-specific multitask heads are retained.

E1.justification: v2 adds 18 DMControl tasks with proprioceptive observations and continuous actions. Multitask Atari coverage expands from four jointly learned games to eight and all 26 games. The original 26-game single-task benchmark and VisualMatch memory-length scenarios remain.

E2.justification: The Atari results table drops IRIS, DreamerV3, STORM, and EfficientZero, and the separate four-way representative-game comparison is removed. MuZero (Reproduced) corresponds to the earlier MuZero w/ SSL. v2 adds MuZero to the multitask comparison and compares against DreamerV3 on DMControl.

E3.justification: v1 Table 6 versus v2 Table 8 reports four versus two transformer layers, value-loss weighting of 0.25 versus 0.5 outside DMControl, and disabled versus periodically enabled Atari reanalysis. v2 introduces continuous-control protocols and larger multitask configurations. Atari aggregate reporting adds the normalized median and removes the superhuman-game count.

E4.justification: v2 adds multitask model-size sweeps and t-SNE representation analysis. It redesigns the Pong depth/context ablation and replaces the VisualMatch depth study at memory length 60 with one at 500. Existing target-network ablations, trajectory examples, and attention-map analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Three-run means and 95% confidence intervals remain the predominant reporting practice. However, v1 Figure 10 explicitly declares these for the VisualMatch depth ablation, whereas its revised counterpart, v2 Figure 16, omits the run count and uncertainty definition. This establishes reduced disclosure, without establishing fewer runs.

E6.justification: The revised Atari table changes UniZero's reported wins from 17 to 15 of 26 games and its normalized mean from 0.433 to 0.39; reproduced MuZero changes from 0.414 to 0.44. These results use revised settings. VisualMatch curves are also replaced. New multitask and DMControl outcomes include Table 3's means of 787.2 for UniZero and 743.7 for DreamerV3.

T1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds formal definitions for the Gaussian continuous policy, proposal distribution, visit-count target, and distillation objective. Section 2 also corrects the regularization expression to compare predicted latent states with stop-gradient observation encodings. No new theorem or proof framework is introduced.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes resolving long-term-memory limitations, with preliminary multitask potential. v2 makes heterogeneous-task scalability central, adds continuous-control performance claims, and claims the first online MCTS-based single model achieving performance comparable to single-task learning across the full Atari 100K benchmark.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies v1's generally favorable interpretation of longer training contexts: benefits depend on prediction accuracy and sufficient transformer depth. It adds a proposed cross-task information-sharing explanation for multitask embedding patterns. The earlier explanation that LayerNorm avoids harmful cross-task BatchNorm statistics is removed.

D1.justification: v2 documents continuous-action implementation and DMControl settings, including 20 sampled actions, action repeat two, and task-specific loss weights. It specifies enlarged multitask models and newly discloses VisualMatch's fixed color mapping. The earlier multitask LayerNorm recommendation disappears. Hardware, reported training times, and LightZero access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work taxonomy and Appendix F comparison largely remain. v2 adds the full-Atari online-MCTS priority claim and citations for DMControl, t-SNE, SimSiam, and Bench2Drive. It also changes the IRIS attribution from Mandlekar et al. to Micheli et al.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, conclusion, and substantial explanatory passages are rewritten around heterogeneous-task scalability. Experiments are reordered to foreground VisualMatch and multitask learning, and the appendices are reorganized. Terminology shifts toward modular components and heads, while citations change from numbered to author-year format.

P2.justification: Architecture and search diagrams are redrawn, and v2 introduces multitask tables, scaling plots, t-SNE visualizations, a median-score chart, and DMControl displays. Ablation panels are regrouped and the Atari table loses comparator columns. Retained case studies are relocated within a substantially reformatted page layout.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens previously tentative generality claims with continuous-action implementation details, DMControl evaluation, and expanded multitask evidence, while qualifying the context-length recommendation. These benefits are tempered by removed Atari comparators and unresolved comparison settings: Table 10 asserts identical settings, but Tables 8-9 specify Atari reanalysis for UniZero and none for MuZero. These issues limit the net quality gain.
